thesis: Western Digital is now a pure-play hard disk drive (HDD) company after spinning off its flash memory business as Sandisk in early calendar 2025. **[Fact]** Customers are cloud hyperscalers, enterprises, and consumer/OEM channels buying capacity enterprise (nearline), mission-critical, and client drives. **[Fact]** Continuing operations revenue was **$9.52 billion** in fiscal 2025 ended June 27, 2025 (+50.6% versus **$6.32 billion** in fiscal 2024 continuing revenue). **[Fact]** Operating profit on continuing operations was **$2.33 billion** (24.5% margin) versus **$403 million** prior year. **[Fact]** Owner cash in fiscal 2025 was approximately **$3.56 per share** after **$1.69 billion** operating cash flow and **$412 million** capital spending, on **359 million** diluted shares. **[Fact]** Western Digital retained a **28.8%** equity stake in Sandisk after the separation.
why_market_wrong: There is **no dated predictive attribute** (HK: **none**). **[Inference]** The market may be extrapolating AI-driven nearline HDD demand as a multi-year supercycle, embedding peak-cycle owner cash and a full valuation of the retained Sandisk stake into WDC's price. **[Inference]** The alternative view is that HDD economics remain cyclical despite the duopoly: cloud digestion pauses, exabyte growth normalizes, and today's price leaves little margin of safety even if near-term earnings stay elevated.
